title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Denials and Appeals by Denial Code
content:
On the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program a denial is worked by its denial code, and the code alone decides the route; the CGM Self-Pay Program has no denials or appeals.

## Route by code

| Denial code | Meaning | Route |
|---|---|---|
| CO-16 | Claim lacks information | Unprocessable and never appealed; cured only by a corrected claim transmitted no later than the tier's corrected-claim window (calendar days) after the denial's posting date |
| CO-50 | Not medically necessary | Appealable |
| CO-151 | Frequency or quantity not supported | Appealable only when a medical record supporting the quantity, dated on or before the date of service, is on file |
| CO-197 | Authorization absent | Appealable only when an authorization grant valid on the date of service is on file |
| CO-29 | Timely filing expired | Never appealed and never billed to the customer; Larkfield writes it off with a billing correction adjustment |
| PR-204 | Not covered under the plan | Becomes the customer's responsibility only under the program's liability notice rule; otherwise Larkfield absorbs it |

A CO-197 or CO-151 denial whose condition in the table is not met is not appealed and is handled as a non-covered amount under the program's liability notice rule.

## Appeal windows and levels

1. A first-level appeal may be filed no later than the tier's first-level appeal window (calendar days) after the posting date of the denial it appeals, counted in calendar days from that posting date with the last day allowed.
2. An appeal decision that upholds the denial posts as a new denial whose original posting is the appeal filing.
3. A second-level appeal may be filed only against such an upheld first-level decision, no later than the tier's second-level appeal window (calendar days) after its posting date. Where that window is 0 there is no customer-filed second level on the tier, and on the CGM Medicare Advantage Program the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity itself.
4. One appeal is filed per level per denial; a denial already appealed at a level is not appealed again at that level.

## Cases (hypothetical figures)

- Suppose a first-level window of 60 days and a denial posted on 1 March of a non-leap year: an appeal filed on 30 April is in time; one filed on 1 May is late.
- A CO-197 denial for a date of service on which a grant was valid is appealable; the same denial for a date of service on which no grant on file was valid is not appealed.
- A CO-151 denial with a supporting medical record dated the day after the date of service is not appealed, because the record must be dated on or before the date of service.
- A CO-50 denial already appealed at the first level cannot be appealed again at the first level.
